outcomes.item: `docs-site/app/dungeonbreak-content-app/asset-explorer/page.tsx` and `docs-site/components/reports/asset-explorer.tsx` now provide a fresh Asset Explorer route with `react-jsonschema-form`-driven create/update flows, searchable form-bound asset lists, and x/y/z numeric plotting for authored collections.

`docs-site/lib/content-editor/payload-content-authoring.ts` now derives item-level asset schemas from supported Escape the Dungeon contract schemas, exposes those supported game forms in project detail, and seeds them into Payload through `docs-site/app/api/content-editor/projects/[projectId]/game-schemas/route.ts`.

The Asset Explorer now treats Escape the Dungeon as the first-class scope: imported canonical pack documents can be searched as asset collections, selected canonical forms show pack/data readiness, and save flows patch the canonical pack document in place instead of forcing everything through generic project-data records.

follow-ups.item: The next active lane is `63-05`: keep Asset Explorer focused on Escape the Dungeon by improving export/publish flow, game-specific widgets/bindings, and the round-trip between Payload canonical assets and the playable game.

`pnpm --dir docs-site run build` is still failing on an existing Next.js server import issue: `docs-site/app/api/mcp/route.ts` pulls `packages/engine/dist/index.js`, which includes a React client component export and triggers a `useEffect/useRef/useState` server import error unrelated to the new Asset Explorer work.
